cohort: The study included 168 patients with uterine malformations undergoing artificial insemination by husband (AIH) and 168 matched controls with infertility but normal uteri.
finding: While clinical pregnancy rates were similar between women with and without uterine anomalies undergoing AIH, those with anomalies experienced higher rates of cancellation, pregnancy loss, and preterm birth, leading to lower term and live birth rates.
